references.context: Commutative algebra: square-zero ideal I of a commutative unital ring A, characterized by I²={0} (equivalently ab=0 for all a,b∈I). The square-zero property is strictly stronger than mere nilpotence of an unspecified positive exponent.
references.reason: The independently reusable square-zero thickening hypothesis is stronger than nilpotent ideal and distinct from the quotient algebra.
references.matching_note: Same contextual concept as previously stored square-zero-ideal candidate missing.16a17500cd760e24ed49; review this additional occurrence for alias equivalence.

references.context: Commutative algebra: quotient ring A/I of a commutative unital ring A by an ideal I, with elements additive cosets a+I, operations induced from A and canonical surjective unital quotient map A→A/I. This includes prime-ideal quotients, polynomial-ring quotients and ideal-power quotients; a quotient's being a field, local ring or R-algebra requires additional conditions.
references.matching_note: This is the ordinary quotient ring by an ideal. Distinct specific features of this occurrence (prime ideal, polynomial base ring, local ring, square-zero ideal or powers) remain in its mathematical source. It is not a general quotient module or a quotient topology.

references.context: Commutative algebra: lift of an R-algebra homomorphism f:S→A/I across a surjective R-algebra map q:A→A/I, namely an R-algebra homomorphism g:S→A satisfying q∘g=f. Here I is square-zero and formal unramifiedness only requires uniqueness, not existence.
references.reason: The notion of a lift through a specified quotient is reusable across formal unramified, étale and smooth lifting criteria; existence and uniqueness must not be conflated.
references.matching_note: The definition imposes at most one lift, not a guaranteed lift; compare with formal smoothness lifting contexts.

references.disposition: Uniqueness is part of the formal-unramified condition.

references.context: General topology: a continuous closed map f:X→Y is one that sends every closed subset F⊆X to a closed subset f(F)⊆Y; no Hausdorff or properness assumptions are implicit.
references.reason: Being a closed continuous map is an independent topological property, distinct from the universal stability of closedness under all base changes.
references.matching_note: Check other closed-map candidate occurrences and distinguish universally closed from merely closed.

references.phrase: topological fibre product with subspace topology
references.context: General topology: pullback X×_Y Z={(x,z)∈X×Z:f(x)=g(z)} equipped with the subspace topology induced by the product topology on X×Z, with canonical continuous projection maps. This realizes the categorical pullback in Top.
references.reason: The explicit subspace/product topology on the set-theoretic pullback is additional concrete structure beyond the general categorical universal property already linked.
references.matching_note: Compare to existing topological fibre-product candidate missing.840e600e35f86bb70875, currently for X×_Y X, without prematurely equating the separate raw records.

references.disposition: No restriction to discrete or compact Z; the closedness condition is stable under all displayed base changes.

references.phrase: automorphism α of x over identity of p(x)
references.context: Category theory of fibred categories: a vertical automorphism α:x→x in a category S over C, invertible in S and satisfying p(α)=id_{p(x)} in C. The base identity condition is part of verticality, not automatic for a general endomorphism of S.
references.reason: Vertical automorphisms are reusable group-theoretic/categorical data in the inertia construction, distinct from field-automorphism groups or general endomorphisms.
references.matching_note: Preserve fibred-category context and invertibility; potential categorical automorphism prerequisite for global audit.

references.disposition: In the newly defined inertia category, this is the definition of an arrow (x,α)→(x′,α′): β:x→x′ in S with βα=α′β, over the required base arrow. It defines the inertia category's own morphisms rather than a further missing object.
Automorphisms are vertical in the fibre; ordinary arrows not preserving base are excluded from the automorphism condition.
